task_message:
Case L41: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 281x281x386 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case L41 is finished and saved.

**Result:** lipomatous soft-tissue tumor segmented with the final mask at **547.3 mL** (v1), spanning axial slices 156–311 (coronal 55–161, sagittal 85–194).

**How I approached it**
- Scanned the volume in axial, coronal and sagittal planes; located a large, encapsulated, fat-isointense mass in the posterior/posteromedial proximal thigh that displaces the hamstrings.
- Prompted nnInteractive with several positive points through the mass in its largest axial cross-section (slice 200), which produced a clean first-pass mask following the dark capsule on axial, coronal and sagittal planes.
- Checked the ends: no discrete lesion tissue at axial 148 or at axial 319 beyond the capsule; coronal/sagittal past-the-end panels were clean.
- Reviewed all automatic candidates (C1–C5): they were subcutaneous fat rim and thin fascial/muscle strips — rejected as normal tissue.
- Tried extending the proximal fat crescent (v2), but the model produced a thin stalk running along the intermuscular fat plane to the hip; I undid that (removing ~71 mL of normal-fat leak) and kept the compact, capsule-following mask.

Confidence is **medium** because the tumor's tapered fatty poles blend with adjacent intermuscular fat, but the boundaries in all three planes otherwise follow the lesion.
